title: Field Evaluation of Low-Cost Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensors under Drip Irrigation

headings.text: Field Evaluation of Low-Cost Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensors under Drip Irrigation

key_sentences: We compared four models of low-cost capacitive soil moisture sensors with gravimetric reference samples over one irrigation season in a semi-arid vegetable plot.
After a site-specific calibration, three of the four models estimated volumetric water content within three percentage points of the reference.
Reference samples were taken twice a week with a soil corer next to each sensor and dried at 105 °C for 24 hours.
Table 1 lists the root mean square error of each model before and after calibration.
Errors were larger in the clay loam than in the sandy loam for every model.

tables.caption: Table 1. Error in volumetric water content (percentage points) for the validation period; failures are sensors that stopped reporting.

list_items.text: (a) Calibrate each model in the soil where it will be used, at least with a two-point procedure.
(b) Seal the electronics and cable entry before installation.
(c) Install the sensor several days before relying on its readings, so that the soil can settle around it.
(d) Replace sensors that show a steady upward drift between irrigations.
[1] Ombasa, R. (2025). Gravimetric sampling protocol for raised beds. Station Methods Note 14.
[2] Fairweather, L. and Valcarce, T. (2024). Logging irrigation events with open hardware. Technical Report TR-24-03.
[3] Dry Hollow Agricultural Research Station (2023). Soil survey of the valley floor plots. Internal report.
